content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

The test image shows a tomato leaf with a large, irregular grayish-brown lesion. Key features:
- Large, roughly angular lesion bounded by leaf veins
- Grayish-brown to tan center with a darker area at top
- Somewhat water-soaked margins around the lesion
- Possible fuzzy sporulation on the lesion surface
- Healthy green surrounding tissue

This pattern is most consistent with **Late Blight** (large water-soaked lesions turning grayish-brown, vein-bounded). Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference images are not accessible at the provided paths. I'll base my classification on the visual analysis of the test image alone.

**Visual Analysis Summary:**
- Large, irregular angular lesion on a tomato leaf (~40% of leaf area)
- Grayish-brown to tan coloration in the lesion center
- Dark greenish-gray area at the top of the lesion (characteristic of sporulation)
- Lesion somewhat bounded by leaf veins
- Water-soaked appearance at the lesion margins
- Surrounding leaf tissue remains green

**Reasoning:**
- The large, water-soaked lesion turning grayish-brown with possible gray sporulation is the hallmark of **Late Blight** (*Phytophthora infestans*)
- The vein-bounded angular shape and the size of the lesion are classic Late Blight characteristics
- Gray Mold (Botrytis) is also possible but typically shows denser, more distinctly fuzzy gray sporulation
- Leaf Mold typically appears on the lower surface with distinct olive-green mold
- Early Blight shows concentric rings (target-like) which are absent here
